issues.description: SR1/SR2 checks only exercise two illegal-jump instances (indices 22 and 26) rather than a broader stress suite; hidden spec mentions 'additional illegal-transition and sticky-invalid stress vectors' but coverage is limited to the two embedded in the fixed stimulus.

Reference-only artifacts are appropriately gated (module names differ from pinned interface, comments state reference-only), but rely on participant discipline not to submit them directly; harness does not explicitly verify submission file is distinct from inputs, though functionally this is enforced by requiring module name quad_decoder.
issues.evidence: module quad_decoder_gates / quad_decoder_wrapper vs required module quad_decoder

recommendations: Consider expanding SR1/SR2 stress coverage to include additional illegal-transition patterns (e.g., back-to-back illegal jumps, illegal jump immediately after reset) to better match the hidden_spec's mention of broader stress vectors.

Optionally add an explicit check in evaluate.py verifying the submitted module name/port list differs from the reference-only module names (quad_decoder_gates/quad_decoder_wrapper) to guard against accidental copy-paste submissions, though current naming already prevents silent acceptance.

requirement_results.evidence: The gate-level netlist faithfully implements the Gray-code decoder described in hidden_spec.ground_truth (current/prev DFFs, XOR compare, decode tree matching Gray adjacency, ripple adder, dir/invalid registers), and the design_brief.md/README.md/metadata.json consistently restate the same pinned interface semantics without contradiction.
requirement_results.requirement: Coherence between public inputs, hidden ground truth, and expected outputs

requirement_results.evidence: baseline_run and golden_run both show exit_code 0 with all PASS; mutation_baseline_run also passes. The vulnerable_run (naive always-zero-like mutant) shows exit_code 1 with FR1, FR2, FR4, SR2 FAIL as expected, confirming the always-zero stub fails FR1/FR2 per task spec.
requirement_results.requirement: Evaluator accepts correct submission and rejects naive baseline

requirement_results.evidence: evaluate.py performs cycle-accurate PROBE comparison against an independent Python reference model covering pos/dir/invalid (word_recovery_rate), FR1-FR4 pass/fail (structural_match_accuracy), and full FR+SR+SR3 boolean pass (functional_equivalence), matching metrics list in task spec.
requirement_results.requirement: Evaluator measures requested metrics (word_recovery_rate, structural_match_accuracy, functional_equivalence)

requirement_results.evidence: requirement_map lists FR1-FR4 as requirement_type functional and SR1-SR3 as requirement_type security, each with distinct expected_detection logic and test file references.
requirement_results.requirement: Requirement map covers functional and security requirements separately

requirement_results.evidence: Testbench explicitly drives two distinct diagonal illegal jumps (00->11 and 10->01) mid-sequence and evaluate.py checks pos/dir hold (SR1) and invalid single-cycle pulse with no re-assertion (SR2) around these specific triggered events, plus SR3 static regex scan for backdoor tokens.
requirement_results.requirement: Security-relevant behaviors actively triggered, not just generically checked

requirement_results.evidence: All referenced files (README.md, metadata.json, inputs/*, submission/recovered_rtl.v, evaluation/*) are provided in the bundles; netlist/wrapper elaborate standalone with local primitive submodules; no external dependencies or unsafe constructs present.

The task is a domain-specific hardware reverse-engineering exercise requiring recovery of word-level RTL from a flattened gate-level Gray-code quadrature decoder netlist, with domain-appropriate artifacts (netlist, wrapper, design brief) and toolchain (iverilog/vvp/yosys).
requirement_results.requirement: Benchmark adapted to domain rather than generic filler

requirement_results.evidence: differential harness shows golden passes and a vulnerable/mutant submission fails on exactly the expected requirements (FR1, FR2, FR4, SR2), mutation_score is 1.0 with all seven requirements having mutants detected, confirming discriminative power of the test harness.

README.md, metadata.json, and inputs/design_brief.md describe FR1-FR4 and general Gray-code/illegal-jump behavior in plain engineering terms; no CWE ids, SR id labels, or explicit statements that the baseline is 'intentionally vulnerable' appear in any public-facing file. The baseline stub comment says only 'intentionally incorrect (it always outputs zero)' framed as a placeholder skeleton, not a security backdoor.
requirement_results.requirement: No leakage of hidden security intent in public-facing artifacts

requirement_results.evidence: Exactly four FRs (FR1-FR4) are defined, each tied to a specific stimulus pattern (forward run, reverse run, stationary/bounce, illegal diagonal jump) and each independently checked via distinct PROBE segment comparisons in evaluate.py, not a single generic restatement.
requirement_results.requirement: Public functional requirements are concrete and machine-checkable (2-4 FRs)
